task_description: Write a method in Dafny that takes in two sequences and subtracts the elements of the first sequence by the elements of the second sequence with the same index.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method SubtractSequences(s1: seq<int>, s2: seq<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The length of the result sequence should be equal to the length of s1 and s2
- Each element in the result sequence is the difference between the corresponding elements of s1 and s2
- For all valid indices i, result[i] == s1[i] - s2[i]
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method SeqSubtract(seq1: seq<int>, seq2: seq<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - Both input sequences should have the same length

Dafny specification:
    requires |seq1| == |seq2|
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The result sequence should contain elements where each element is the corresponding element of seq1 minus the corresponding element of seq2

Dafny specification:
    ensures |result| == |seq1|
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |result| ==> result[i] == seq1[i] - seq2[i]
    
Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method SeqSubtract(seq1: seq<int>, seq2: seq<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
    requires |seq1| == |seq2|
    ensures |result| == |seq1|
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |result| ==> result[i] == seq1[i] - seq2[i]
{
    var res := [];
    var i := 0;
    while i < |seq1|
        invariant 0 <= i <= |seq1|
        invariant |res| == i
        invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> res[j] == seq1[j] - seq2[j]
    {
        res := res + [seq1[i] - seq2[i]];
        i := i + 1;
    }
    result := res;
}
```
